info.title: Omnigraph API
info.description: HTTP API for the Omnigraph graph database

get.summary: List every graph currently registered with this server.
get.description:
Multi-graph mode only. In single mode, the route returns 405 — there's
no registry to enumerate. Cedar-gated by the server-level policy via
the `graph_list` action against `Omnigraph::Server::"root"`.

Order: alphabetical by `graph_id` (server-sorted so clients see
deterministic output across requests).
Returns branch names sorted alphabetically. Read-only.

parameters.name: graph_id
parameters.description: Graph id to route the request to.

post.description:
Forks `name` off of `from` (defaults to `main`). The new branch shares
table data with its parent until it is mutated. Returns 409 if `name`
already exists.

parameters.name: graph_id
parameters.description: Graph id to route the request to.

429.description: Per-actor admission cap exceeded; honor `Retry-After` header

503.description: An overlapping durable recovery intent must be resolved before retry

post.description:
Merges `source` into `target` (defaults to `main`). Outcome is one of
`already_up_to_date`, `fast_forward`, or `merged`. Returns 409 with the
list of conflicts if the merge cannot be completed; the target is left
unchanged in that case. **Destructive** to `target` on success.

With `delete_branch: true` the source branch is deleted after a successful
merge, under its own `branch_delete` policy check. The merge is durable by
then, so a deletion refusal or failure never fails the request; it is
reported via `branch_deleted: false` + `branch_delete_error`.

delete.description:
**Irreversible.** Removes the branch pointer; commits remain reachable
only if referenced by another branch. Returns 404 if the branch does not
exist.

get.description:
`branch` selects which history to list: a named branch returns the history
reachable from that branch's head (the main commits inherited up to the
fork plus the branch-authored commits); omitting it returns `main`'s
history. There is no cross-branch listing. Ordering is part of the
contract — newest first by (manifest version, created-at, commit id) — and
a future `cursor`/`limit` pagination will be keyset-based on that same
order. Read-only.

parameters.name: graph_id
parameters.description: Graph id to route the request to.

post.summary: Stream the contents of a branch as NDJSON.
post.description:
Emits one JSON object per line (`application/x-ndjson`). Filter with
`type_names` (node/edge type names) and/or `table_keys`; both empty
streams the entire branch. Suitable for large exports — the response is
streamed, not buffered. Read-only.

Bulk-load NDJSON data into a branch. Behavior is unchanged; the route is

`POST /load`, which has identical semantics. Responses from this route
include `Deprecation: true` and `Link: <load>; rel="successor-version"`
headers per RFC 9745 / RFC 8288 so SDKs and proxies can surface the signal.

post.summary: Bulk-load NDJSON data into a branch (canonical load endpoint).
post.description:
`data` is NDJSON with one record per line. `mode` controls behavior on
existing rows: `merge` upserts by id (default), `append` strictly inserts
absent ids, and `overwrite` replaces table contents. Branch creation is opt-in by
presence of `from`: with `from` set, a missing `branch` is created from
it; without `from`, `branch` must already exist — a missing branch is a
404, never an implicit fork. **Destructive** when `mode` is `overwrite`
or when the load produces conflicting writes.

The legacy `POST /ingest` route has identical semantics and is kept as a
deprecated alias.

parameters.name: graph_id
parameters.description: Graph id to route the request to.

post.summary: Apply a GQ mutation to a branch (canonical mutation endpoint).
post.description:
Writes to the named `branch` (defaults to `main`). Mutations are atomic
per call and produce a new commit. Returns counts of nodes and edges
affected. **Destructive**: on success the branch is updated; rejected
mutations may still acquire locks briefly. Returns 409 when the prepared
write authority changes before effects.

Pairs with `POST /query` (read-only). The legacy `POST /change` route
has identical semantics and is kept as a deprecated alias.

get.summary: List the graph's exposed stored queries as a typed tool catalog.
get.description:
Returns every stored query in the `queries:` registry, each
with its MCP tool name, read/mutate flag, description/instruction, and
typed parameters — enough for a client to register them as tools without
fetching `.gq` source. Cluster-served graphs have no per-query expose flag,
so the catalog lists them all. Read-gated; the catalog is graph-wide (branch
independent — `read` is authorized against `main`). **Not** Cedar-filtered
per query yet, so it can list a query whose `invoke_query` the caller
lacks (a known gap until per-query authorization lands).

parameters.name: graph_id
parameters.description: Graph id to route the request to.

200.description: Stored-query catalog (every stored query, with typed params)

post.summary: Invoke a curated, server-side stored query by name.
post.description:
The query source comes from the graph's `queries:` registry, not the
request body — callers send only runtime inputs (`params`, `branch`,
`snapshot`). Gated by the `invoke_query` Cedar action at the boundary;
a stored *mutation* additionally passes the engine's `change` gate
(double-gated). An actor **without** `invoke_query` cannot tell a denied
query from a missing one — both return the same 404, so the catalog
can't be probed without the grant. Once `invoke_query` is held, the
inner `read`/`change` gate may surface a 403 for an existing query the
actor can't run (the intended double-gate signal).

parameters.name: graph_id
parameters.description: Graph id to route the request to.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Stored query name (the registry key)

200.description: Read envelope (ReadOutput) or mutation envelope (ChangeOutput), serialized untagged

400.description: Bad request (param type error; snapshot on a stored mutation)

403.description: Forbidden (the inner `change` gate for a stored mutation)

404.description: Unknown stored query, or `invoke_query` denied — indistinguishable to a caller without the grant

413.description: Stored keyed mutation exceeds the per-commit row or byte ceiling

429.description: Per-actor admission cap exceeded; honor `Retry-After` header

500.description: Policy evaluation error (a denial is reported as 404, not 500)

503.description: A stored mutation is blocked by a durable recovery intent

post.summary: Execute an inline read query (friendlier-named alternative to `POST /read`).
post.description:
Designed for ad-hoc exploration and AI-agent tool-use: short field
names (`query`, `name`) match the CLI `-e` flag and the GQ `query`
keyword. Mutations (`insert`/`update`/`delete`) are rejected with 400
-- use `POST /mutate` (or its deprecated alias `POST /change`) for
write queries. Otherwise behaves identically to `POST /read`: same
target semantics (branch xor snapshot), same Cedar action (Read),
same response shape.

parameters.name: graph_id
parameters.description: Graph id to route the request to.

400.description: Bad request - also returned when the query body contains mutations; use POST /mutate (or its deprecated alias POST /change) for write queries

post.description:
Execute a GQ read query. Behavior is unchanged from prior releases; the
route is kept indefinitely for byte-stable back-compat. New integrations
should target `POST /query`, which has clean field names (`query` /
`name`) and a 400-on-mutation guard. Responses from this route include
`Deprecation: true` and `Link: <query>; rel="successor-version"`
headers per RFC 9745 / RFC 8288 so SDKs and proxies can surface the
signal.

get.description:
Returns the project's schema as a single string in `.pg` source form.
Useful for clients that want to introspect available types and tables
before constructing GQ queries. Read-only.

parameters.name: graph_id
parameters.description: Graph id to route the request to.

post.description:
Cluster-backed servers reject this route with `409 Conflict`; operators
must apply schema changes through `omnigraph cluster apply` and restart.

Diffs `schema_source` against the current schema and applies the resulting
migration steps (add/drop type, add/drop column, etc.). **Destructive**:
some steps drop data. Returns the list of steps applied; if `applied` is
false the diff was unsupported and no changes were made.

parameters.name: graph_id
parameters.description: Graph id to route the request to.

409.description: Schema apply is disabled for cluster-backed serving; use `omnigraph cluster apply` and restart

get.summary: Read the current snapshot of a branch.
get.description:
Returns the manifest version plus per-table metadata (path, version, row
count) for every table on the branch. Defaults to `main` when `branch` is
omitted. Read-only.

parameters.name: graph_id
parameters.description: Graph id to route the request to.

post.summary: Ingest a graph-native NDJSON firehose through the checked served runtime.
post.description:
A request without `If-Match` is authorized and preflighted without polling
its body, then receives a 428 challenge. A malformed or stale precondition
receives 412 without replacement authority. An exact strong ETag transfers
the Axum body stream directly into the engine and streams one redacted
newline-delimited result per input row; neither direction is buffered as a
complete request or response.

parameters.name: graph_id
parameters.description: Graph id to route the request to.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: Strong ETag containing the opaque graph token returned by the 428 challenge.

requestBody.description: Graph-native node and edge rows, one JSON object per line. Results are emitted in caller order and the request is not atomic.

409.description: Checked streaming runtime or lifecycle conflict

412.description: Malformed or stale graph token; no replacement token is disclosed

428.description: Graph token required; retry with the strong ETag in If-Match

ETag.description: Strong ETag containing the current opaque graph token

503.description: Overlapping durable recovery must resolve before ingest

get.summary: Return one coherent, graph-redacted streaming operational cut.
get.description:
This is graph-wide read metadata, so Cedar authorizes it with `read`
rather than the mutation-capable `stream_manage` action. The engine bridge
already removes every table, lane, binding, shard, epoch, generation,
dataset, and recovery identity before the transport receives the value.

parameters.name: graph_id
parameters.description: Graph id to route the request to.

Cache-Control.description: Always `no-store`; the response contains live advisory state and compare revisions

409.description: The current server does not own checked status authority for this profile state

413.description: The bounded status inventory exceeded its hard observation envelope

500.description: Checked status failed without exposing physical diagnostics

503.description: A stable checked cut could not be obtained; retry

get.description:
Returns server status and version. Unauthenticated; safe to call from any
caller. Use this to confirm the server is reachable before invoking other
endpoints.

from.description: Parent branch to fork from. Defaults to `main`.

name.description: Name of the new branch. Must not already exist.

branch_delete_error.description:
Why the requested source-branch deletion did not happen. Present iff
`branch_deleted` is `false`.

branch_deleted.description:
Result of the requested post-merge source-branch deletion. Absent when
`delete_branch` was not requested; `true` when the source branch was
deleted; `false` when the deletion was refused or failed (the merge
itself still succeeded — see `branch_delete_error`).

delete_branch.description:
Delete the source branch after a successful merge. The deletion runs
under its own `branch_delete` policy check; a refusal or failure is
reported via `branch_deleted` / `branch_delete_error` on the response
and never fails the already-landed merge.

source.description: Source branch whose commits will be merged.

target.description: Target branch that will receive the merge. Defaults to `main`.

name.description:
Name of the mutation to run when `query` declares multiple.

Accepts the legacy field name `query_name` as a deserialization alias.

params.description: JSON object whose keys match the mutation's declared parameters.

query.description:
GQ mutation source containing `insert`, `update`, or `delete` statements.
May declare multiple named mutations; pick one with `name`.

Accepts the legacy field name `query_source` as a deserialization alias.

created_at.description: Commit creation time as Unix epoch microseconds.

oneOf.description:
Set when a strict keyed insert found an existing or concurrently
inserted logical id.  The caller may choose a different id; replaying
the same strict operation will not convert it into an upsert.

Set when the conflict is a publisher CAS rejection
(`ManifestConflictDetails::ExpectedVersionMismatch`). The caller's
pre-write view of `table_key` was at version `expected` but the
manifest is now at `actual`. Refresh and retry.
Set when a prepared write's logical authority changed before effects.

Set when an overlapping durable recovery intent must be resolved before
retry. Its table effects may or may not have started.

Set when the request must be split into smaller graph commits. The
rejected attempt has no durable sidecar and no table effect.

table_keys.description: Restrict the export to these table keys. Empty exports all tables.

type_names.description: Restrict the export to these node/edge type names. Empty exports all types.

GraphInfo.description:
One entry in the response from `GET /graphs`. Cluster operators
consume this list to discover which graphs the server is currently
serving. The shape is intentionally minimal — `graph_id` and `uri`
are the only fields a routing client needs.

GraphListResponse.description:
Response from `GET /graphs`. Lists every graph registered with the
server in alphabetical order by `graph_id` (sorted server-side so
clients get deterministic output across requests).

internal_schema_version.description: The internal-schema (storage-format) version this binary writes and reads.

base_branch.description:
Base branch a fork was requested from (the request's `from`), echoed
even when the branch already existed. `null` when `from` was absent.

branch.description:
Target branch. Defaults to `main`. Without `from`, the branch must
already exist — a missing branch is a 404, never an implicit fork.

data.description:
NDJSON payload: one record per line, each shaped
`{"type": "<TypeName>", "data": {...}}`.

from.description:
Parent branch used to create `branch` if it does not exist. Branch
creation is opt-in by presence of this field; omit it to require an
existing branch.

oneOf.description: How existing rows are handled. Defaults to `merge`.

InvokeStoredQueryRequest.description:
Body for `POST /queries/{name}` — invokes the server-side stored query
named in the path. The query source and name come from the registry,
never the body; only the runtime inputs are supplied here.

branch.description:
Branch to run against. Defaults to `main`; for a stored mutation the
write targets this branch.

expect_mutation.description:
The kind the caller expects: `Some(false)` for
`omnigraph query <name>`, `Some(true)` for `omnigraph mutate <name>`.
When set and it disagrees with the stored query's actual kind, the
server rejects the call (400) so the verb asserts the kind. `None`
(the default) skips the check — preserving older clients and aliases.

params.description: JSON object whose keys match the stored query's declared parameters.

snapshot.description:
Snapshot id to read from (read queries only — rejected for a stored
mutation). Mutually exclusive with `branch`.

InvokeStoredQueryResponse.description:
Response for `POST /queries/{name}`: the read envelope for a stored
read, or the mutation envelope for a stored mutation. Serialized
**untagged**, so the wire shape is exactly [`ReadOutput`] or
[`ChangeOutput`] — classification follows the stored query, not a
wrapper field.

LoadMode.description: Shadow enum for documenting [`LoadMode`] in the OpenAPI schema.

ManifestConflictOutput.description:
Structured details for a publisher-level OCC failure. Surfaces alongside
HTTP 409 when a write was rejected because the caller's pre-write view of
one table's manifest version was stale relative to the current head. The
expected/actual fields tell the client which table to refresh.

ParamDescriptor.description: One declared parameter of a stored query, projected for the catalog.

oneOf.description:
Element kind when `kind == list` (always a scalar — the grammar
forbids lists of vectors or nested lists).

nullable.description: `false` → the caller must supply it; `true` → optional.

ParamKind.description:
The kind of a stored-query parameter, decomposed so a client (e.g. an
MCP server) can build a typed input schema with a closed `match` and
never re-parse omnigraph's type spelling. `bigint`/`date`/`datetime`/
`blob` are carried as JSON strings on the wire: a 64-bit integer past
2^53 loses precision as a JSON number, and Date/DateTime are ISO
strings, Blob a blob-URI string.

QueriesCatalogOutput.description:
Response for `GET /queries`: every stored query in a graph's
registry, each with typed parameters.

QueryCatalogEntry.description: One entry in the stored-query catalog (`GET /queries`).

mutation.description: `true` for a stored mutation → an MCP read-only hint of `false`.

QueryRequest.description:
Inline read-query request for `POST /query`.

Friendlier-named alternative to [`ReadRequest`] for ad-hoc reads and
AI-agent integration. Mutations are rejected with 400 — use `POST
/mutate` (or its deprecated alias `POST /change`) for write queries.
Field names are deliberately short (`query`, `name`) to match the GQ
keyword and the CLI `-e` flag.

branch.description: Branch to read from. Mutually exclusive with `snapshot`. Defaults to `main`.

name.description:
Name of the query to run when `query` declares multiple. Optional when
only one query is declared.

params.description: JSON object whose keys match the query's declared parameters.

query.description:
GQ read-query source. May declare one or more named queries; pick one
with `name` when more than one is declared. Mutations
(`insert`/`update`/`delete`) get 400 — use `POST /mutate` (or its
deprecated alias `POST /change`) instead.

snapshot.description: Snapshot id to read from. Mutually exclusive with `branch`.

branch.description: Branch to read from. Mutually exclusive with `snapshot`. Defaults to `main`.

params.description: JSON object whose keys match the query's declared parameters.

query_name.description:
Name of the query to run when `query_source` declares multiple. Optional
when only one query is declared.

query_source.description:
GQ query source. May declare one or more named queries; pick one with
`query_name` if there is more than one.

snapshot.description: Snapshot id to read from. Mutually exclusive with `branch`.

ReadSetConflictOutput.description:
Structured authority mismatch for a prepared write. Values are
strings because members include optional graph commit ids and future
authority tokens, not only numeric table versions.

ResourceLimitOutput.description:
A write rejected before durable recovery ownership because its bounded
physical plan exceeded an explicit row, byte, or transaction-chain ceiling.

allow_data_loss.description:
When true, promote every `DropMode::Soft` step in the plan to
`DropMode::Hard`, making the prior column data unreachable
after the apply. Matches the CLI's `--allow-data-loss` flag.
Defaults to `false` (drops remain reversible via time travel).

schema_source.description:
Project schema in `.pg` source form. The diff against the current
schema produces the migration steps that will be applied.

internal_schema_version.description:
The on-disk internal-schema (storage-format) version this graph's branch
is stamped at.

StreamDeclarationOutput.description: Logical schema declaration with streaming state.

StreamDeclarationStatusOutput.description: Checked status for one logical node or edge declaration.

StreamDrainStatusOutput.description: Active drain operation for one logical declaration.

StreamDriverStateOutput.description:
Process-local fold-driver run state. Driver health is advisory and never
substitutes for durable lifecycle or recovery authority.

StreamDriverStatusOutput.description: Advisory health of the fold driver serving this graph.

StreamIngestChallenge.description:
Effect-free precondition challenge for graph-native streaming ingest.

The same value is returned as a strong `ETag` response header. Clients
retry the request with that tag in `If-Match`; this convenience copy keeps
the graph authority token distinct from the per-row sequencing
[`StreamIngestLineOutput::stream_token`].

StreamIngestKindOutput.description: Logical declaration kind selected by one graph-native stream row.

StreamIngestLineOutput.description:
One ordered, newline-delimited result from graph-native streaming ingest.

Every field is caller-logical or directly actionable retry evidence.
Physical table and MemWAL identities are deliberately absent.

current_token.description: Current per-row token returned with a sequencing or terminal outcome.

stream_token.description: Confirmed per-row sequencing token. This is not the graph-level ETag.

unconfirmed_candidate_token.description: Candidate token whose durability acknowledgement is unknown.

StreamIngestScopeOutput.description:
Whether one stream result applies to a single row or blocks the graph-wide
remainder of the request.

StreamIngestStatusOutput.description:
Stable, graph-logical status vocabulary for one streaming-ingest line.

Several private physical-authority transitions intentionally collapse to
`stream_authority_changed`; the transport never exposes lane, binding,
shard, epoch, generation, dataset, or recovery-sidecar identity.

StreamLastFoldStatusOutput.description:
Most recent durable fold summary, with physical operation and generation
coordinates removed.

StreamLifecycleOutput.description: Stable graph-level lifecycle state for one logical declaration.

StreamPendingStatusOutput.description:
Pending acknowledged work for one logical declaration.

Counts are returned only when the checked status cut can observe them
without claiming a writer or advancing replay state. An unavailable result
names only the graph-safe reason classes; it never exposes a shard,
generation, dataset, or recovery operation.

StreamRebuildBlockerOutput.description: One graph-safe reason an export/import rebuild is not currently allowed.

StreamRebuildStatusOutput.description:
Whether the checked graph cut can be rebuilt without discarding streaming
sequencing authority.

StreamStatusOutput.description: One coherent, graph-redacted operational status cut.

enrolled_declarations.description:
Logical node/edge declarations whose streaming state has initialized.
Absence here does not mean the graph schema has no declarations.

StreamStrictBlockStatusOutput.description: Current strict validation block for one logical declaration.

StreamTokenCountsOutput.description:
Current graph-wide sequencing-authority counts. Generic status deliberately
omits the sampled logical IDs and per-key stream tokens used by the
internal proof.
